instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the noodles.

Meanwhile, make the curry paste. Roughly chop 2 of the shallots and the 6 garlic cloves. Peel about 1 inch of the ginger and slice it. Put them in a food processor with a small handful of cilantro stems and leaves (about 1/4 cup), the zest of 1 lime, 2 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp curry powder and 2 tbsp shrimp paste.
Blend until smooth, stopping to scrape down the sides. If the blades spin without catching, add a tablespoon of water.
Slice the 1 lb chicken thighs into thin bite size strips and sprinkle them with the 1/2 tsp salt.

Get the toppings ready. Thinly slice the other 2 shallots, chop a handful of the cilantro, and cut both limes into wedges. Roughly chop the pickled mustard greens. Put them in small bowls with the chili paste for the table.

Pour 1/2 cup of the oil into a small skillet over medium-high. When a strand of noodle sizzles hard as soon as it goes in, fry a small handful of the noodles (about 2 oz) for 30 seconds to 1 minute, turning them with tongs, until golden and crisp. Lift them onto paper towels. Stand back a little. The oil will spatter.
Heat the other 2 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium-high. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until it's browned in spots. It doesn't need to be cooked through yet. Move it to a bowl.
Turn the heat to medium and scrape the paste into the fat left in the pot. Fry it for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring all the time, until it turns a shade darker and smells toasty.
Stir in 2 tbsp red curry paste and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the carton of broth, add the 2 tsp brown sugar and scrape up anything stuck to the bottom. Bring it to a boil.
Turn the heat down so it bubbles gently. Stir in the can of coconut milk and 3 tbsp fish sauce. Keep it at a gentle bubble from here on. A hard boil can split the coconut milk.

Put the chicken and its juices back in and simmer for 5 to 6 minutes. You're cooking it to 175°F, so if you have a thermometer, check a thick piece. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Meanwhile, cook the rest of the noodles in the boiling water as the package says, usually 2 to 3 minutes, until tender. Drain them well.
Taste the broth. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lime.

Divide the noodles between 4 deep bowls, ladle the chicken and broth over and top each one with the crispy noodles. Serve with the sliced shallots, pickled mustard greens, cilantro, lime wedges and chili paste on the side.
method_notes: Both versions fry a curry base in fat until fragrant, build it into a coconut milk broth seasoned with fish sauce and sugar, cook the chicken in it, and serve it over boiled egg noodles with crispy fried noodles, shallots, pickled mustard greens, lime and chili on top. The Woks of Life blends a fresh paste of shallot, garlic, ginger, cilantro, lime zest, turmeric, coriander, curry powder and shrimp paste, adds canned red curry paste and stock, and browns sliced thighs first. Hungry in Thailand cracks thick coconut milk until the oil separates, fries red curry paste and curry powder in it and simmers whole drumsticks for 20 to 30 minutes. This one follows The Woks of Life with its bird's eye chilies left out of the paste, so the heat is the chili paste at the table.
